oewn-00672179-v.learner: to think carefully about someone or something and decide how good or bad it is
examples: You must give me leave to judge for myself, and pay me the compliment of believing what I say.
But everybody is to judge for themselves

oewn-00973682-v.learner: to state a decision you have made about someone or something
examples: The doctor judged her fit to return to work.

oewn-00674352-v.learner: to make a rough guess about how much there is of something, or how long something takes
examples: I judged the distance to the house to be about a mile.

oewn-06779826-n.learner: something you say after thinking it over carefully
examples: had some new extracts to admire and some new observations of threadbare morality to listen to
This observation would not have prevented her from trying to talk to the latter

oewn-00881437-n.learner: the act of watching someone or something in a patient, unhurried way
examples: at Longbourn there would be leisure enough for observation
the observation of a very few minutes convinced her that she was only exceedingly shy

oewn-05711376-n.learner: the act of noticing something, or giving your attention to it
examples: The change in her manner escaped his observation.

oewn-01013569-v.learner: to state seriously and firmly that something is true
examples: He protested that she should receive from him no mark of affection whatever on the occasion.
Mrs. Philips protested that they would have a nice comfortable noisy game of lottery tickets

oewn-02527076-v.learner: to show that you are against something by what you do or by what you say
examples: she had meant to encourage him by protesting against his proposals

oewn-00912088-v.learner: to say words that show you object to something
examples: The boy protested that she should not; she continued to declare that she would

oewn-07144758-n.learner: a thing that someone has said
examples: To this speech Bingley made no answer
that speech savours strongly of disappointment

oewn-07125165-n.learner: the passing of spoken words back and forth between people
examples: Away ran the girls, too eager to get in to have time for speech.

oewn-07253354-n.learner: the act of giving a formal talk to a group of listeners
examples: Her cousin prefaced his speech with a solemn bow
with a bow to Mr. Darcy, he concluded his speech, which had been spoken so loud as to be heard by half the room

oewn-09357302-n.learner: the firm surface of the earth that we walk and stand on
examples: It was a large, handsome stone building, standing well on rising ground

oewn-09201896-n.learner: a sensible reason for believing something or for doing something
examples: She had no grounds for thinking that he would come back.

oewn-14867162-n.learner: the loose soft stuff that covers much of the land
examples: He dug a hole in the ground and set the young tree in it.

oewn-07564444-n.learner: a deep, bitter anger and bad feeling towards someone
examples: Nor did that day wear out her resentment.
Mr. Darcy seemed to catch her words with no less resentment than surprise.

connotation.why: names anger held and nursed against someone rather than plain anger

oewn-00125649-v.learner: to come little by little into some state, or to take on some quality; to become
examples: She grew absolutely ashamed of herself.
she cannot grow many degrees worse

oewn-00251067-v.learner: to develop until you are fully formed and adult
examples: With three younger sisters grown up, your Ladyship can hardly expect me to own it.

oewn-00231172-v.learner: to get bigger, greater, or more than before
examples: The crowd outside the inn grew larger as the evening went on.

oewn-06694296-n.learner: a short telling of what has happened
examples: a report soon followed that Mr. Bingley was to bring twelve ladies and seven gentlemen with him to the assembly
pretend to be affronted at an idle report

oewn-07232584-n.learner: the act of telling people about something by speaking
examples: We learned of the accident only through her report.

oewn-07233130-n.learner: a written paper setting out what a person or a group has found out
examples: The committee published its report on the state of the roads.

oewn-00175261-n.learner: an action you take as part of getting closer to something you want
examples: To be fond of dancing was a certain step towards falling in love
this false step in one daughter will be injurious to the fortunes of all the others

oewn-04322052-n.learner: one of the flat places you rest your foot on when going up or down a stairway
examples: When they ascended the steps to the hall, Maria's alarm was every moment increasing

oewn-00286401-n.learner: the act of moving by lifting your foot and putting it down again
examples: He took a step towards the door and then stopped.

oewn-02009962-v.learner: to get to the place you were going to
examples: When Mr. Bennet arrived, he had all the appearance of his usual philosophic composure.
a letter arrived from Mrs. Gardiner

oewn-02591952-v.learner: to become very successful and reach the top
examples: After years of small parts, she felt she had finally arrived.
